name: Art Deco product
summary: Rich, geometric objects of the jazz age: stepped forms, fans and sunbursts in chrome, ebony, lacquer, mirror and Bakelite, made by hand and by machine for a city luxury.

philosophy.core_thesis: Luxury can be geometric: a rare material, a precise machine line and a bold pattern make an object that looks rich and modern.
design_principles: Build each form from stepped tiers, a fan, a sunburst or a chevron; repeat it three to five times.
Use rare, dark wood such as Macassar ebony and rosewood with a high French polish.
Pair a dark ground with a bright metal: chrome, nickel or gilt brass on ebony, black glass or lacquer.
Cut glass and mirror in facets; etch or frost glass in a geometric pattern.
Keep the outline symmetrical about a vertical axis, with a strong base and a stepped top.
Use Bakelite and other new plastics for knobs and cases, moulded in a sharp, faceted form.
Set each pattern in a rhythm of 3 to 5 equal parts, and make each surface a mirror or a deep gloss.
anti_patterns: Rough, hand-hewn timber and visible tool marks
Plain white, bare steel with no pattern
Plastic that looks cheap, in a toy colour

form.geometry: Stepped pyramids, fans, sunbursts, chevrons and zigzags, built on a strict symmetrical axis.
form.silhouette: A stepped, symmetrical outline with a wide base and a narrow top, like a skyscraper in small scale.
form.edges: Crisp, faceted edges and bevels with a radius of 0 to 3 mm; a few large rounded corners of 20 to 50 mm on a case.
form.proportion: A sideboard is about 1.8 times wider than high; a table lamp is about 40 cm high, with a base and a shade of equal width.
form.ornament: Geometric inlay, fluting, sunburst and chevron; it covers 15 to 40% of the surface and repeats in 3 to 5 steps.
rules: Each object is symmetrical about one vertical axis.
A stepped form has 3 to 5 tiers, and each tier is about 60 to 80% of the width of the tier below it.
A pattern repeats in equal parts: a fan has 5 to 9 rays.
A dark ground and a bright metal meet at a sharp line.
Surfaces are polished to a mirror or a deep gloss.

materials.rule: Dark wood, glass and metal share the surface in about equal parts; textile is a rich, dense pile.

finish.gloss: 80–100 GU on wood, lacquer and metal
finish.patina: The style wants a new, deep shine; a worn or dull surface loses the effect.

hardware.section: Rods and stems 10–20 mm, handles 12–25 mm, base discs 60–120 mm
hardware.joints: Fine, tight joints; a polished metal band or a flush mount hides each seam, and a screw head is flush or covered.
hardware.handles: A stepped bar, a ring or a faceted knob in chrome, ebony or Bakelite, with a section of 12 to 25 mm.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A faceted or stepped Bakelite push button; a tap with a ribbed, faceted or stepped lever in chrome.

palette.strategy: A dark, rich ground with a bright metal and one jewel colour: black, ebony brown, chrome, gold, with jade or ruby.

manufacture.scale: Luxury workshops made single pieces and small series; large firms made the same forms in machine series for the shop and the home.
manufacture.signs: Tight veneer matches in a mirror image, sharp bevels, a chrome band at each edge and a mould parting line that is polished away.

objects.form: fan or shell in frosted glass
glass top on a sculptural base

positive: macassar ebony with a high polish

canonical_works.work: Furniture of the Hôtel du Collectionneur

emotion.target_response: Confident glamour: the viewer sees a rich, precise object and feels the pace of the city.

use_cases: lighting and hardware for a hotel or a cocktail bar
a brief for a deco reissue
a still life with mirror and chrome
hardware schedules for a period flat
avoid_when: The room needs a rustic or a quiet, natural look.
The brief asks for a matt, raw or recycled finish.

modifiers.how: Round each corner, drop the stepped tiers and use long horizontal lines in chrome and aluminium.
Remove the pattern and the rare wood; keep chrome, opal glass and plain solids.
Keep the geometry, but use laminate, pastel and a loud pattern.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object that quotes the fan, the step and the gloss keeps the style.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Exposition internationale des arts décoratifs et industriels modernes
